figs.title: Turbofan h-s diagram: work and jet energy
figs.caption: On h-s axes the turbine enthalpy drop from 4 to 5 equals the compressor rise plus the bypass ratio times the fan rise. The remaining drop from total to static at each nozzle exit is V²/2, so the core jet at 9 and the slower, larger bypass jet at 19 read straight off the diagram.

figs.title: Best range and endurance points on the polar
figs.caption: For a parabolic polar the three figures of merit peak at C_L*/√3, C_L* and √3C_L*, where C_L* = √(C_D0/K). A jet cruises for range at the lowest C_L, a propeller aircraft cruises at (L/D)_max, and a propeller aircraft loiters at the highest C_L, where induced drag is three quarters of the total.

figs.title: Absolute and service ceilings
figs.caption: Maximum rate of climb falls with altitude as thrust lapses and the excess power shrinks. The absolute ceiling is where it reaches zero, and the service ceiling is where it equals 0.5 m/s (100 ft/min).

figs.title: CG envelope and the fuel burn path
figs.caption: Loading payload and then wing fuel walks the CG along curves on the weight versus CG chart, and the flight burns back down the fuel curve. Every point of the path stays between the forward limit from elevator authority and the aft limit from the minimum static margin, and a tail trim tank moves the cruise CG aft at constant weight.

figs.title: Aileron reversal and control effectiveness
figs.caption: Aileron deflection twists the wing nose down, which removes part of the lift it adds, so effectiveness falls as (1 − q/q_R)/(1 − q/q_D). It reaches zero at the reversal dynamic pressure q_R, which depends on torsional stiffness and the aileron moment and is independent of the offset that sets divergence.
